title: Enclosures, Sealing & IP
description: Enclosure review covering architecture, ingress protection and sealing, environmental durability, drop, EMC and electronics integration, thermal, safety, battery compartments, user interface and cleanability.

items.text: Split lines between housings are placed so they do not cross sealing paths, cosmetic surfaces or user grip zones unnecessarily
items.hint: Review split lines on the industrial design model with sealing and cosmetics in view. A badly placed split line forces a complex gasket or a visible step.

items.text: Mating housings locate to each other with defined locating features rather than fasteners or outer edges
items.hint: Use pins, bosses or perimeter tongue-and-groove features tied to the datum scheme. Locating on screws gives variable alignment.

items.text: Housing-to-housing step and gap at the split line are specified and achievable with the locating scheme
items.hint: Run the step and gap stack around the perimeter. Cross-reference the Tolerancing checklist for the analysis method.

items.text: A lip, tongue or overlap at the split line hides the gap and blocks a direct line of sight into the enclosure
items.hint: A straight butt joint shows every mismatch and gives a direct path for light, dust and probes.

items.text: Lids, doors and covers are retained so that they stay closed under drop, vibration and pressure conditions
items.hint: Check the latch or fastener retention force against the loads. Doors that pop open in a drop expose batteries and electronics.

items.text: Large flat walls have enough stiffness (ribs, curvature or thickness) to avoid oil-canning, rattles and seal gaps
items.hint: Check wall deflection under the expected handling and internal loads by hand calculation or FEA. A flexible wall between fasteners opens the seal gap.

items.text: PCBs are supported by bosses or ribs close enough together to limit board flex during assembly, connector mating and drop
items.hint: Check support spacing near heavy parts and connectors that are pushed by users. Coordinate support locations with EE keep-outs.

items.text: PCB mounting is not over-constrained, so housing tolerance or thermal expansion does not bend the board
items.hint: Use one fixed point and slotted or compliant others, or check the induced board strain. Board flex cracks ceramic capacitors and BGA joints.

items.text: Mounting provisions for the product (wall, DIN rail, VESA, tripod, panel cut-out) are defined and load-rated
items.hint: Check the mounting interface against the customer specification and the load with a safety factor. Cross-reference Thermal & Structural Analysis for the load case.

items.text: Internal space claims for components, cables and air paths are reserved and checked with the latest EE and supplier CAD
items.hint: Import the latest PCBA STEP and component models and run interference and clearance checks. Stale EE models are a common source of late conflicts.

items.text: The IP rating target per IEC 60529 is defined for the product and for each opening, including service and battery doors
items.hint: List every opening (split lines, buttons, connectors, vents, windows, speaker ports, doors) with its target rating and sealing method. An opening without an owner is the one that leaks.

items.text: Every seal path is continuous around the full perimeter with no gaps, butt joints or unsupported spans
items.hint: Trace the sealing line in CAD around each opening, including where it passes bosses and corners. Check the gasket or bead is supported along its whole length.

items.text: Gasket compression stays within the gasket supplier's recommended range across worst-case tolerances
items.hint: Run the stack for minimum and maximum compression. Too little leaks; too much takes a compression set or overstresses the housing.

items.text: Seal path corners have radii that the gasket can follow without wrinkling or lifting
items.hint: Check the minimum inner radius against the gasket supplier's guidance for the cross-section. Sharp corners are the usual leak points.

items.text: Gasket groove fill stays below the gasket supplier's maximum at maximum gasket and minimum groove volume
items.hint: Elastomers are nearly incompressible; an overfilled groove forces material out or prevents closing. Include thermal expansion of the gasket at maximum temperature.

items.text: A compression stop (hard stop) limits gasket compression so the clamping load goes into housing metal-to-metal or plastic-to-plastic contact
items.hint: Without a hard stop, compression depends on screw torque and plastic creep. Check that the stop is reached before the gasket is overcompressed.

items.text: Fastener spacing and housing stiffness give even gasket compression between fasteners
items.hint: Check housing deflection between fasteners under the gasket reaction force using FEA or a beam calculation. Gaps open midway between widely spaced screws.

items.text: O-ring glands follow the O-ring supplier's handbook for gland depth, width, squeeze and stretch
items.hint: Check static or dynamic gland dimensions, squeeze and stretch percentages, and lead-in chamfer against the handbook for the chosen cross-section and material.

items.text: O-rings are protected from cutting during assembly by lead-in chamfers and the absence of sharp edges or cross holes they pass over
items.hint: Trace the O-ring path during assembly. Threads, port edges and parting lines it crosses must be chamfered or covered.

items.text: Sealing faces have a specified surface finish compatible with the seal type
items.hint: Specify the roughness on the drawing per the seal supplier. Texture, tool marks or ejector pins on a sealing face create leak paths.

items.text: No parting line, gate, ejector mark or weld line crosses a sealing face
items.hint: Review mold flow and tooling layout against the seal path. A parting-line flash across a seal face is a classic leak and tooling-change cause.

items.text: Formed-in-place or dispensed gaskets have a defined bead size, path and cure, and a dispensing supplier has confirmed the geometry
items.hint: Check minimum bead start/stop overlap, corner radii and groove shape with the dispensing material supplier.

items.text: A membrane vent equalizes internal pressure where altitude, temperature changes or sealed volume would otherwise load the seals
items.hint: Sealed enclosures pump air through the weakest seal as they heat and cool. Size the vent airflow and water entry pressure per the vent supplier.

items.text: Membrane vents are protected from direct jets, debris and mechanical damage and can be sealed to the housing reliably
items.hint: Place vents in sheltered locations and specify the bonding surface finish and flatness required by the vent supplier.

items.text: Buttons and switches have a seal (membrane, boot, O-ring or overmold) rated for the IP target and the actuation cycle life
items.hint: Check that the seal remains intact over the full actuation count and that actuation force includes the seal's stiffness.

items.text: External connectors are sealed by a rated sealed connector, a panel gasket or a cover, with the mated and unmated states considered
items.hint: Define the IP rating for each connector both mated and unmated. Connector supplier ratings apply only with the specified panel cutout and gasket.

items.text: Cable entries use rated cable glands or overmolded strain reliefs sized for the actual cable diameter range
items.hint: Check the gland's clamping range against the cable OD tolerance and the panel thickness and hole size required.

items.text: Windows, lenses and labels bonded over openings use an adhesive seal with a continuous, defined bond width
items.hint: Specify the die-cut tape or adhesive bead with minimum bond width per the tape supplier, and the bonding pressure.

items.text: Water that enters non-sealed zones (between outer cosmetic parts and the sealed core) drains out and does not pool against seals
items.hint: Trace where spray or rain collects in the use orientations and add drain paths. Standing water defeats seals designed for splash.

items.text: Potting or encapsulation, where used, has a defined volume, fill level, cure, and compatibility with components and housing
items.hint: Check the potting compound's shrinkage, CTE and cure stress on components, and that air can escape during fill. Potting makes rework impossible; confirm the decision.

items.text: Exposed plastics and elastomers are UV-stabilized grades rated for the expected outdoor exposure
items.hint: Check UV stability data per material datasheet. Unstabilized plastics chalk, yellow and embrittle; the gasket will fail long before the housing.

items.text: Condensation inside the enclosure is managed by venting, desiccant, conformal coating or drainage
items.hint: Sealed enclosures that cycle through the dew point collect water. Decide the strategy with EE and document it.

items.text: All exposed metals and fasteners have corrosion protection suitable for the environment (salt spray, humidity, chemicals)
items.hint: Check finish and material against the environment class. Cross-reference Materials & Finishes for the finish specification.

items.text: Seals remain compliant across the full operating and storage temperature range
items.hint: Check the elastomer's low-temperature limit and compression set at high temperature per datasheet. Stiff seals at low temperature leak.

items.text: Dissimilar materials in the enclosure are checked for differential thermal expansion at temperature extremes
items.hint: Large plastic-to-metal joints shift with temperature and can open seals or crack bosses. Calculate the expansion difference at extremes.

items.text: Openings and surfaces exposed to dust, sand, ice or insects are protected against blockage and damage
items.hint: Check vents, drain holes and moving parts for clogging. Ice formation in recesses can jam buttons and doors.

items.text: Housing corners and edges that hit first in a drop are reinforced or protected by bumpers
items.hint: Identify likely impact points from the drop orientations. Add wall thickness, ribs or an elastomer bumper and check by drop simulation or prototype.

items.text: Heavy internal parts (motors, magnets, speakers, ballast) are retained so they cannot break loose or load the PCB in a drop
items.hint: Trace each heavy part's load path to the housing. Calculate inertial load from the drop deceleration estimate or simulation.

items.text: Displays, cover glass and touch panels are supported around their perimeter and isolated from housing flex
items.hint: Check the support area, bonding tape and gap to the housing. Glass breaks where it bears on a hard point or edge.

items.text: Cover glass and lenses are recessed or have a raised housing bezel so a flat-surface drop does not hit the glass first
items.hint: Check the bezel height above the glass at all edges with tolerances.

items.text: Ribs, screw tips and sharp edges near the battery keep enough clearance that a drop cannot dent or puncture the cell
items.hint: Check the clearance at worst-case tolerance plus housing deflection from drop simulation. Cell damage is a fire and safety issue.

items.text: Snap fits and latches on the enclosure stay engaged under drop loads
items.hint: Check the latch retention force against inertial loads on the latched part. Lids popping open in a drop is a common first-test failure.

items.text: Shielding requirements (shield cans, conductive coating, conductive gaskets) are agreed with EE and represented in CAD
items.hint: Confirm which housing areas must be conductive and how continuity is made at seams. Late shielding additions often need tooling changes.

items.text: Conductive paint or plating areas have masking defined on the drawing, coordinated with EE contact points
items.hint: Show coated and masked areas in a drawing view. Paint where a gasket or ground contact needs bare metal kills the ground path.

items.text: Grounding contact points between PCB, chassis and shields are defined with spring contacts, gaskets or fasteners and a controlled contact surface
items.hint: Check spring contact compression range across tolerances per the contact supplier. Specify bare or plated contact areas.

items.text: Antenna areas keep the clearance from metal parts, metallic paint, fasteners and conductive coatings that EE and the antenna supplier specify
items.hint: Overlay the antenna keep-out on the housing CAD, including in-mold decoration, metallic inks and fasteners.

items.text: ESD discharge paths from user-accessible seams, buttons and connectors lead away from sensitive circuits
items.hint: Review seams near the PCB edge, button gaps and connector shells with EE. Increase creepage paths at seams or provide a deliberate discharge path to ground.

items.text: Light pipes are aligned with their LEDs within tolerance and optically isolated from neighbors
items.hint: Run the LED-to-light-pipe stack. Add light-blocking ribs or opaque materials between adjacent indicators to prevent crosstalk.

items.text: Display windows have a defined viewing area, black-mask border and gap to the display that avoids pressure marks
items.hint: Check that the visible area aligns with the active area across tolerance, and that the window cannot touch the display when pressed.

items.text: Button actuators line up with their switches across tolerances and actuate them at the center
items.hint: Run the actuator-to-switch stack in X, Y and Z. Off-center actuation gives a mushy feel and short switch life.

items.text: Connectors on the PCB are accessible through the housing openings with correct alignment and depth across tolerances
items.hint: Check the opening-to-connector stack and that the mating plug seats fully before its overmold hits the housing.

items.text: Any conflict between ventilation openings and the IP target is resolved with a documented approach
items.hint: Options include sealed heat paths to the housing, membrane vents, labyrinth vents or a lower rating for part of the enclosure. Record the decision.

items.text: Heat paths from hot components to the housing (thermal pads, gap fillers, heat spreaders) have defined compression and contact area
items.hint: Check gap filler compression across tolerances against the supplier's range, and that the PCB is not overstressed by the pad force.

items.text: Vent openings, fans and air paths are not blocked by the product's mounting, users' hands or nearby surfaces in intended use
items.hint: Check vent placement against all use orientations and mounting. Cross-reference Thermal & Structural Analysis for the thermal model.

items.text: Housing materials near heat sources are rated for the local temperature over the product life
items.hint: Compare the local temperature to the material's heat deflection and long-term temperature rating per datasheet.

items.text: Enclosure materials meet the flammability rating required by the applicable safety standard (e.g. a UL 94 class) at the actual wall thickness
items.hint: UL 94 ratings depend on thickness. Check the material's yellow card at the thinnest wall of the enclosure.

items.text: Openings in the enclosure prevent access to hazardous parts as checked with the standard's test probes
items.hint: Model the applicable probe (e.g. the test finger) and check it against every opening and gap. Include gaps that open under the probe force.

items.text: Access to hazardous voltages, moving parts or hot parts requires a tool, or is interlocked
items.hint: Check every cover that exposes a hazard is tool-only or interlocked, per the applicable standard.

items.text: Mains or external power cords have strain relief and anti-rotation that meet the applicable standard's pull and torque tests
items.hint: Check the strain relief design and that it cannot be pushed into the enclosure. Plan a pre-compliance pull test.

items.text: Creepage and clearance distances that depend on mechanical parts (housing ribs, barriers, insulating sheets) are maintained across tolerances and assembly variation
items.hint: Get the required distances from EE and check them in CAD at worst case, including after a drop or applied force.

items.text: The battery compartment has a vent path that directs gas away from the user in a cell failure
items.hint: Follow the cell supplier's and the safety standard's guidance. A fully sealed battery compartment can turn a cell failure into a burst housing.

items.text: The compartment allows for cell swelling over life per the cell supplier's data without stressing the housing or PCB
items.hint: Leave the swelling allowance in the thickness direction for pouch cells. Swelling pushes displays and housings apart in the field.

items.text: Battery polarity is enforced mechanically for user-installed cells or packs
items.hint: Keyed shapes, polarity-specific contacts or a reversed-insertion block. Mark polarity clearly as well.

items.text: Battery contacts provide the required contact force over the life and tolerance range, and resist corrosion
items.hint: Check spring contact deflection range across cell size tolerance per the contact supplier.

items.text: The battery door or cover stays closed in a drop and resists opening by children where the regulations or market require it
items.hint: Check the applicable child-resistance requirements for coin cells and button batteries. Verify door retention under drop load.

items.text: Battery packs are retained in all directions with features that do not bear on the cell's weak areas
items.hint: Avoid loads on pouch cell seals and terminals. Use foam, brackets or a tray as the cell supplier recommends.

items.text: Button travel and actuation force meet the UI specification across tolerances, including the seal and actuator contribution
items.hint: Build a force-travel budget combining switch, dome, membrane and actuator stiffness. Confirm on prototypes.

items.text: Buttons have a defined tactile response and do not rattle or stick in their openings
items.hint: Check the clearance between button and housing across tolerances, and that the button cannot rotate or catch on an edge.

items.text: Button and interface labels (printed, molded, laser-etched) are durable for the expected wear and cleaning
items.hint: Check abrasion resistance for the marking method against the use profile.

items.text: Backlit features and indicators do not leak light around button edges or through thin walls
items.hint: Check wall opacity and add light-blocking features. Light leakage at seams is a common cosmetic rejection.

items.text: Controls cannot be actuated accidentally by normal handling, carrying or placing the product on a surface
items.hint: Check recess depth or guards for critical buttons. Accidental actuation is a usability and sometimes safety issue.

items.text: External surfaces can be cleaned with the specified method without crevices, deep recesses or seams that trap contamination
items.hint: Review seams, button gaps and texture for areas a wipe cannot reach. Minimize exposed fasteners and gaps.

items.text: Enclosure materials and seals are resistant to the specified cleaning and disinfecting agents over the required number of cycles
items.hint: Check chemical resistance per datasheet and plan chemical exposure testing under stress. Many plastics crack under the combination of disinfectant and molded-in stress.

items.text: Openings and seals in cleaned areas keep cleaning fluid out of the enclosure
items.hint: Check the seal design against the cleaning method (spray, wipe, immersion) and the fluid's surface tension, which is lower than water's.

items.text: Skin-contact surfaces have no sharp edges, pinch points or features that snag hair or skin
items.hint: Inspect radii and gaps on all contact surfaces. Check moving parts such as straps and clasps for pinch points.
